description: Willem de Kooning established his reputation as a key figure in the Abstract Expressionist movement with a series of black-and-white paintings in the late 1940s. These works marked the artist’s shift from a figurative drawing style to the evolving gestural tradition of the New York School. The resulting works embodied the physical act of painting, a defining characteristic that would become known as “action painting.”
